resources.string: Persistent notification for network quality downgrade
Samples every %1$d s and downgrades automatically when the criteria are met
Off — the network mode will not be changed automatically
Master switch (on by default). On: when fake full bars or weak signal is detected, 5G is switched to 4G automatically; Off: samples and logs only, the network mode is never changed
In dBm (default -85). RSRP must be above it to count as a strong signal and to be able to trigger fake full bars; higher values are stricter and harder to trigger

In dB (default 0). Only checked when the signal is strong: SINR below it counts as poor quality, and higher values are stricter. If SINR cannot be read, this criterion is skipped and Ping is used instead
In ms (default 200). Only checked when the signal is strong: Ping above it counts as poor quality, and lower values are stricter and trigger more easily
Count complete ping failure as poor
Off by default. On: if every ping fails it also counts as poor quality and still downgrades; Off: logged only, no downgrade. Enable it only if probes often fail completely
On by default. On: when RSRP falls below the weak signal threshold below, it switches to 4G; Off: weak signal is only recorded and the network mode stays unchanged
In dBm (default -110). RSRP below it counts as a weak signal, regardless of Ping or SINR; it only takes effect while the switch above is on, and higher values downgrade more easily
Off by default. On: EN-DC (NSA dual connectivity) is also disabled while downgrading and restoring, which some devices need in order to actually fall back to 4G; leave it off if you are not sure
Defaults to 4G preferred. The network mode written when a rule is met; 4G only is more thorough but drops the 3G fallback, so in areas with poor coverage it may end up with no service at all

Defaults to follow carrier. The network mode written back when the cooldown ends and the network is restored; it is derived automatically from the SIM card as 5G auto, so swapping SIMs needs no changes. Choosing the wrong one may leave 5G unavailable after restoring
In s (default 60 = 1 minute). No restore is attempted for this long after a downgrade, so it does not bounce straight back to 5G; a longer cooldown saves more power but brings 5G back more slowly

In rounds (default 2). After the cooldown ends, this many consecutive healthy rounds are required before restoring; a larger value is more stable but slower, while 1 lets a single jitter trick it back to 5G

In rounds (default 2). After a downgrade, this many consecutive rounds with no network at all roll everything back to the full network mode; a smaller value recovers faster, a larger one tends to stay stuck offline
In s (default 60). The foreground service samples this often; a larger value saves power but reacts more slowly. Opening the monitor page temporarily speeds it up to 5 s
Restores monitoring and the downgrade state after a reboot
